findings.title: Use datetime-aware cursor keys for audit-log pagination
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`, but this implementation uses the generic numeric key conversion. On a nonempty first page, cursor construction calls `math.floor()` on a `datetime`, which raises `TypeError`; subsequent pages would also pass an integer cursor value to a datetime field filter. Requests opting into this paginator therefore fail instead of returning audit logs. Preserve the date conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative offsets cause Django queryset slicing to fail
findings.body: When advanced pagination is enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch evaluates a queryset slice with a negative start. Django does not support negative queryset indexes and raises `ValueError`, turning the request into a server error. Negative offsets can be supplied in a cursor; implement reverse paging using valid slices or reject them before slicing.

findings.title: Changing span-buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks live Redis data
findings.body: This writes sorted sets under the same `span-buf:s:*` keys that previous versions stored as Redis sets. During a rolling deploy, or while old buffered segments remain, `ZADD` against an existing set fails with `WRONGTYPE`; the new Lua `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` and flush-time `ZSCAN` operations also fail on those keys. New and old consumers cannot safely share these keys, so ingestion or flushing can stall until the old keys expire. Use versioned keys or migrate existing data before switching types.

findings.title: The shorter redirect traversal limit can split deep segments
findings.body: This loop now follows only about 1,000 redirect links before using the current `set_span_id` as the destination. For a deeper span hierarchy, that value may not be the segment's root, so the new span is stored under an intermediate key and can be flushed as part of the wrong segment. Redirect chains can outlive the 1,000 retained payloads because eviction does not remove their mappings. Retain a sufficient traversal bound or detect exhaustion and resolve the chain safely.

findings.title: The max_segment_spans setting is no longer enforced
findings.body: The load-time check against `self.max_segment_spans` has been removed, while the insertion script uses a hard-coded limit of 1,000. A caller configuring a lower limit can now receive segments up to 1,000 spans, and a caller configuring a higher limit still loses spans at 1,000. Preserve the constructor's configured limit by passing it to the script or enforcing it when loading.

findings.title: Add coverage for the new destructive eviction behavior
findings.body: The added buffer tests supply timestamps but do not create a segment larger than 1,000 spans or assert which spans survive eviction. Since this code intentionally removes stored payloads, add tests for the cardinality boundary, eviction ordering, and eviction while merging buffers; otherwise regressions can silently drop the wrong spans or fail to enforce the cap.
